svg.text: Carrier board for the 30-pin ESP32 DevKit V1 (Bruno)
Top view (component side) of a 5 x 7 cm perfboard, 18 x 24 holes. Antenna end up, USB socket at the bottom edge. Wires are soldered on the underside.
The second header row lands in column 17 or 18, depending on your board. ESP32 outline is approximate.
solid line: bare wire or solder bridge along the holes, underside
dashed curve: insulated wire, underside, joined only at its two ends
black dot: a component leg or wire end goes in this hole
Where each ESP32 pin goes (count from the antenna end, EN column)
R1 220 Ω, then LED connector (long leg side)
yellow wire to R2 1 k, then Q1 base
red: 5 V IN connector, and red wire up to C1 / R3
col 2 row 6 to col 6 row 6 (wire link if the motor is rated 5 V)
legs in col 2: C row 12, B row 13, E row 14
2N2222 / PN2222 / 2N3904 / S8050: flat face towards the ESP32
BC337 / BC547: flat face towards the board edge
col 3 row 10 to col 6 row 10, stripe at col 6
+ leg col 2 row 4, – leg (stripe) col 1 row 4
black col 3 row 8, red col 4 row 8
long leg col 2 row 17, short leg col 1 row 17
col 2 row 20 and col 1 row 20 (either way round)
+5 V col 2 row 24, GND col 1 row 24 (from the PowerBoost)
• Plug the two header strips onto the ESP32 first, then solder them: the board sets the row spacing.
• The EN-side header goes in column 8 with its last pin (USB end) on row 24.
• Connectors: 2-pin JST-XH (2.5 mm pitch) or 0.1 inch pin headers. JST-PH does not fit perfboard.
• Solder low parts first: resistors and diode, then Q1, connectors, C1 last.
• Check with a meter before plugging the ESP32 in: no beep between 5 V IN + and GND.
